exposure: early life oxygen therapy (within first week)
vicinity to major roadway (traffic-related air pollution)
cohort: The study involved 3,770 children (mean age 9.1 years, range 5.68-12.16 years; 51.9% boys) enrolled in the Elementary School Student Cohort (2009-2014) from Ulsan University Hospital, Korea.
finding: Early life oxygen therapy and breastfeeding were significant perinatal factors influencing the development of asthma, and these factors also showed combined effects with other risk factors like environmental tobacco smoke, traffic-related air pollution, parental allergic disease, and atopy.
